docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: SeaDoc Specification describes the .sdoc document format and the data structures of supported nodes. Each node reference explains its fields, child structure, and examples.

docs.title: Reading Order
docs.text:
1. Start with the SeaDoc Document Model to understand the file format, node hierarchy, and common fields.
  2. Read Text for text leaves and formatting marks.
  3. Explore Block Elements, starting with Paragraph and Heading, then follow the references for lists, containers, and other blocks.
  4. Explore Inline Elements for Link, Image, File Link, and SeaDoc Link.

docs.title: SeaDoc Document Model
docs.text: This page describes the SeaDoc document format, node hierarchy, and element types. Follow the links to individual node pages for detailed data structures.

docs.title: Document Format
docs.text:
SeaDoc documents stored on disk use format_version: 4 and have the following structure:

{
  "version": 1,
  "format_version": 4,
  "elements": [],
  "last_modify_user": "user@example.com"
}

All four fields are required:

  • version: document revision number.
  • format_version: document format version, currently 4.
  • elements: list of top-level element nodes.
  • last_modify_user: last modifying user, or an empty string when no user is available.

cursors belongs to runtime collaboration responses and is not stored in the .sdoc file.

docs.title: Node Structure
docs.text:
A SeaDoc document is a tree with three node categories:

  1. Document root: the document itself, containing top-level element nodes in its elements property.
  2. Element nodes: containers holding other element nodes or text nodes in their children property.
  3. Text nodes: leaf nodes containing text content and optional formatting marks.

Every element and text node requires a non-empty string id that is unique within the document. Consumers must not require a particular UUID or slug format.

docs.title: Element Nodes
docs.text:
Element nodes can be block elements, which form separate blocks of content, or inline elements, which flow with text inside a block. Both groups include non-void and void elements.

All element nodes, including void and non-void elements, have:

  • id (required, string): unique node identifier.
  • type (required, string): element type.
  • children (required, array): child nodes.

Element-specific fields, including any data object, are documented on the corresponding element pages.

docs.title: Non-Void Elements
docs.text:
Non-void elements expose their child content for editing. Examples include:

  • Block elements: paragraph and blockquote.
  • Inline elements: link.

docs.title: Void Elements
docs.text:
Void elements are treated as a single unit rather than exposing their children as editable text. Examples include:

  • Block elements: divider and formula.
  • Inline elements: image and sdoc_link.

Block and inline void elements still have children. Most, including block void elements and inline images, contain an empty text leaf as a structural placeholder, with visible content stored in element properties. File links and SeaDoc links can retain their display names in text children. Those stored labels are not editable child content; void elements do not require every persisted text child to be empty.

For example, a divider has the following structure:

{
  "id": "element-id",
  "type": "divider",
  "children": [
    {
      "id": "placeholder-id",
      "text": ""
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Text Nodes
docs.text:
A text leaf has:

  • id (required, string): unique node identifier.
  • text (required, string): displayed text.

Text leaves do not require type or children. For example:

{
  "id": "text-id",
  "text": "Text content"
}

See Text for the full text node documentation, including supported formatting marks.

docs.title: Element Types
docs.text:
The following element types are documented here. Some types share a reference page. Existing SeaDoc implementations may support additional types.

  1. blockquote
  2. callout
  3. check_list_item
  4. code_block
  5. divider
  6. embed_link
  7. file_link
  8. formula
  9. header1 through header6
  10. image
  11. image_block
  12. link
  13. multi_column
  14. ordered_list
  15. paragraph
  16. sdoc_link
  17. subtitle
  18. table
  19. title
  20. unordered_list
  21. video
  22. whiteboard

docs.title: Blockquote
docs.text: blockquote is a block element node that represents quoted content, citations, or references.

docs.title: Usage and Children
docs.text:
• Its children contain block elements, commonly paragraphs, headings, lists, and checklist items. A blockquote can contain more than one block.
  • Text and inline elements belong inside those child blocks, rather than directly inside the blockquote.
  • When code blocks or tables are pasted into a blockquote, the editor places those elements outside the quote.

docs.title: Data Structure
docs.text:
{
  "id": "awGPshsHSry9cQJuKxvHGg",
  "type": "blockquote",
  "children": [
    {
      "id": "VVKieoeQRa-b8UP-AxnVIg",
      "type": "paragraph",
      "children": [
        {
          "id": "JT6oOyplQm-270FdGw_M-A",
          "text": "Quote content"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Callout
docs.text: callout is a block element node that represents emphasized content with a background color and an optional icon.

docs.title: Usage and Children
docs.text:
• Its children contain block elements such as paragraphs, headings, checklist items, lists, and blockquotes. Inline content belongs inside those child blocks.
  • A new callout commonly starts with a paragraph. The editor rejects pasted code blocks and tables; a pasted callout's wrapper is removed when inserting it into another callout.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
• style (required, object): callout style.
  • style.background_color (required, string): CSS background color. The editor-created default is #fef7e0; other CSS color values are supported.
  • callout_icon (optional, string): one of trumpet (📢), bulb (💡), prohibited (🚫), or warning (⚠️). An absent field or an empty string means no icon is shown. Store the icon key, rather than the emoji character.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
  "id": "callout-id",
  "type": "callout",
  "style": {
    "background_color": "#fef7e0"
  },
  "children": [
    {
      "id": "callout-paragraph-id",
      "type": "paragraph",
      "children": [
        {
          "id": "callout-text-id",
          "text": "Callout content"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Checklist Item
docs.text: check_list_item is a block element node that represents a checklist item with a completion state.

docs.title: Children
docs.text:
• Its children directly contain text nodes and supported inline elements, such as links.
  • Each checklist item is its own block.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: • checked (required, boolean): completion state. The editor-created default is false.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
  "id": "check-list-id",
  "type": "check_list_item",
  "checked": false,
  "children": [
    {
      "id": "check-list-text-id",
      "text": "Checklist content"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Code Block
docs.text: code_block is a block element node that represents source code across one or more lines.

docs.title: Usage and Children
docs.text:
• Its children are code_line block elements. Each code line contains text nodes representing one line of code, rather than paragraph or inline link elements.
  • Pasted content is converted into code-line text.
code_block -> code_line -> text leaf

docs.title: Required Properties
docs.text: • language (required, string): language identifier, such as javascript, rather than the display label Javascript. Common values include plaintext, bash, css, c, cpp, csharp, go, html, javascript, java, json, php, python, ruby, sql, swift, typescript, xml, and yaml.

docs.title: Optional Properties
docs.text:
• style (optional, object): code display settings.
  • style.white_space (optional, string): nowrap disables visual line wrapping; normal enables it. Visual wrapping does not create additional code_line nodes. When the style object is absent, the editor uses nowrap.

docs.title: Editor-Created Defaults
docs.text:
• language may be an empty string or plaintext when no programming language is set. The historical value text also represents plain text.
  • style.white_space is nowrap for a newly-created block.

language is the native .sdoc field.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
  "id": "code-block-id",
  "type": "code_block",
  "language": "javascript",
  "style": {
    "white_space": "nowrap"
  },
  "children": [
    {
      "id": "code-line-one-id",
      "type": "code_line",
      "children": [
        {
          "id": "code-text-one-id",
          "text": "const value = 1;"
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "code-line-two-id",
      "type": "code_line",
      "children": [
        {
          "id": "code-text-two-id",
          "text": "console.log(value);"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Divider
docs.text: divider is a block element node that represents a horizontal divider. It is a void element and has no additional properties.

docs.title: Children
docs.text: • Its children contain one empty text node as a structural placeholder, rather than editable content. See Void Elements.

docs.title: Data Structure
docs.text:
{
  "id": "divider-id",
  "type": "divider",
  "children": [
    {
      "id": "divider-placeholder-id",
      "text": ""
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Historical documents may contain type: "hr". New documents use type: "divider". Compatibility and migration behavior may depend on the reader implementation.

docs.title: Embed Link
docs.text: embed_link is a block element node that embeds content from an external service, such as SeaTable or Figma. It is a void element.

docs.title: Children
docs.text: • Its children contain one empty text node as a structural placeholder. The embedded content is identified by link and link_type, rather than editable child text. See Void Elements.

docs.title: Required Properties
docs.text:
• link (required, string): non-empty, absolute HTTP(S) URL of the embedded resource.
  • link_type (required, string): embed provider. Current values are seatable and figma.

docs.title: Optional Properties
docs.text:
• data (optional, object): saved display settings. It can be omitted when no height is saved.
  • data.height (optional, number): positive, finite display height in CSS pixels (px), without a unit suffix in JSON. When omitted, the editor uses 300px.

For display, the editor clamps positive saved heights to 300–550 pixels. Non-positive saved heights fall back to 300px. Historical saved values may fall outside this display range.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
  "id": "embed-link-id",
  "type": "embed_link",
  "link": "https://www.figma.com/file/example",
  "link_type": "figma",
  "data": {
    "height": 400
  },
  "children": [
    {
      "id": "embed-link-placeholder-id",
      "text": ""
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: File Link
docs.text: file_link is an inline element node that references a non-SeaDoc file, such as a .md or .txt file. It is a void element.

docs.title: Children
docs.text: • Its children contain a text node storing the filename. The editor treats the link as a single unit; the stored filename is not ordinary editable child text.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
• doc_uuid (required, string): referenced file identifier.
  • title (required, string): filename.
  • display_type (required, string): one of text_link (filename only), icon_link (file icon and filename), or card_link (file card). The insertion command creates icon_link by default.

Writers must persist one of these three display modes. For compatibility, a missing or empty display_type is displayed as a text link by the editor; this fallback is different from the insertion default.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
  "id": "afLKcmNdR4ii2ZqvH8PP8w",
  "type": "file_link",
  "doc_uuid": "c24cee20-88c2-4dba-beb9-4032c5e2c3e1",
  "title": "aaa.txt",
  "display_type": "text_link",
  "children": [
    {
      "id": "bKfw6ms4QlqUf1J5aFCr4w",
      "text": "aaa.txt"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Formula
docs.text: formula is a block element node that represents a mathematical formula. It is a void element whose formula source is stored in data.formula.

docs.title: Children
docs.text: • Its children contain one empty text node as a structural placeholder. The formula source is stored in data.formula, rather than in editable child text. See Void Elements.

docs.title: Required Properties
docs.text:
• data (required, object): formula data.
  • data.formula (required, string): TeX/LaTeX math source passed to the editor's MathJax renderer, such as E = mc^2 or \frac{a}{b}. Store the math source without surrounding $, $$, \(, or \[ delimiters. Backslashes must be escaped in JSON, for example "\\frac{a}{b}". An empty string has no visible formula content; supported commands depend on the reader's MathJax configuration.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
  "id": "formula-id",
  "type": "formula",
  "data": {
    "formula": "E = mc^2"
  },
  "children": [
    {
      "id": "formula-placeholder-id",
      "text": ""
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Heading
docs.text: header1 through header6 are block element nodes that represent six levels of headings.

docs.title: Usage and Children
docs.text:
• Their children directly contain text nodes and supported inline elements, such as links. Content following a heading remains in sibling blocks, rather than becoming its children.
  • The editor moves images out of header1 through header6 into a following paragraph.

docs.title: Data Structure
docs.text:
{
  "id": "G1opTnrHRr6aX7qbJXZJiw",
  "type": "header1",
  "children": [
    {
      "id": "D_bLOntqQHSZ8lu9VJn_JQ",
      "text": "header content"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Image
docs.text: image is an inline element node that represents an image. It is a void element. For an image displayed on its own line, see Image Block.

docs.title: Children
docs.text: • Its children contain one empty text node as a structural placeholder. The image source and link settings belong in data; see Void Elements.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
The image element has:

  • data (required, object): image data.
  • data.src (required, string): non-empty image source, commonly a document asset path such as /image.png or an absolute image URL. Asset paths are resolved using the reader's document asset context; they are not necessarily paths relative to the documentation site.
  • data.file_uuid (optional, string): associated image file identifier.
  • data.href (optional, string): absolute HTTP(S) link target for the image. An absent field or an empty string means the image has no hyperlink.
  • data.linked_wiki_id (optional, string): target wiki ID for a wiki-page image link.
  • data.linked_wiki_page_id (optional, string): target wiki page ID for a wiki-page image link.

docs.title: Inline Image Example
docs.text:
{
  "id": "image-id",
  "type": "image",
  "data": {
    "src": "/image.png",
    "href": "https://cloud.example.com/wikis/wiki-id/page-id/",
    "linked_wiki_id": "wiki-id",
    "linked_wiki_page_id": "page-id"
  },
  "children": [
    {
      "id": "image-placeholder-id",
      "text": ""
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Image Block
docs.text: image_block is a non-void block element node that displays one inline image on its own line.

docs.title: Usage and Children
docs.text:
• Its children contain one inline image, with text leaves before and after it for cursor placement. These leaves can be empty; consumers must not require an image_block to contain only one child.
  • The editor converts an image_block containing multiple images into a paragraph.

docs.title: Data Structure
docs.text: image_block uses the common element fields. Image source and link settings belong to its child Image.

docs.title: Image Block Example
docs.text:
{
  "id": "image-block-id",
  "type": "image_block",
  "children": [
    {
      "id": "before-image-id",
      "text": ""
    },
    {
      "id": "image-id",
      "type": "image",
      "data": {
        "src": "/image.png"
      },
      "children": [
        {
          "id": "image-placeholder-id",
          "text": ""
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "after-image-id",
      "text": ""
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Link
docs.text: link is an inline element node that represents a hyperlink to a URL, a document element, or a wiki page. It is a non-void element with editable link text.

docs.title: Children
docs.text:
• Its children contain one or more text nodes forming the link label. Separate leaves can carry different formatting marks.
  • Its label is editable child content; it does not contain block elements.

docs.title: Required Properties
docs.text:
• href (required, string): absolute HTTP(S) URL target. It may be an empty string when linked_id or linked_wiki_page_id supplies the target.
  • title (required, string): display title.

docs.title: Optional Properties
docs.text:
• linked_id (optional, string): target element ID for an in-document link. Editor-created links use an empty string when no element target is set.
  • linked_wiki_page_id (optional, string): target wiki page ID. Editor-created wiki links use an empty string when no page target is set.

docs.title: Link Targets
docs.text:
At least one of href, linked_id, or linked_wiki_page_id must be a non-empty string. title and text children are display content, not target identifiers.

Link kind Non-empty target field Example URL link href { "href": "https://example.com", "linked_id": "", "linked_wiki_page_id": "" } In-document link linked_id { "href": "", "linked_id": "target-element-id", "linked_wiki_page_id": "" } Wiki page link linked_wiki_page_id { "href": "", "linked_id": "", "linked_wiki_page_id": "target-page-id" }

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
  "id": "link-id",
  "type": "link",
  "href": "https://example.com/docs",
  "title": "SeaDoc documentation",
  "linked_id": "",
  "linked_wiki_page_id": "",
  "children": [
    {
      "id": "link-text-id",
      "text": "SeaDoc documentation"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: List
docs.text: ordered_list and unordered_list are block element nodes that represent numbered lists and bulleted lists. Each list item is represented by a list_item structural element.

docs.title: Children
docs.text:
• Their children normally contain list_item elements. Text and inline elements belong inside each item's child blocks, rather than directly inside the list.
  • A new list_item starts with a paragraph. It can also contain nested ordered_list or unordered_list blocks and code blocks.

The normal structure is:

ordered_list / unordered_list -> list_item -> paragraph -> text or inline elements

docs.title: Ordered List
docs.text:
{
  "id": "S927zAqWQHOkmLEvFespbw",
  "type": "ordered_list",
  "children": [
    {
      "id": "AW53tbxhQYu-HfoSNTfVxQ",
      "type": "list_item",
      "children": [{
        "id": "FZq5VuH8SM-_lE_UKI2GUw",
        "type": "paragraph",
        "children": [
          {
            "id": "NS1OQ71aQ0-VfxtMyqtszw",
            "text": "ordered list 1"
          }
        ]
      }]
    }, 
    {
      "id": "c-GkcbFsS3uuYNtMgsg2mQ",
      "type": "list_item",
      "children": [{
        "id": "PUoT91gOSoS8hB-HObsD1g",
        "type": "paragraph",
        "children": [
          {
            "id": "QEA-1fOPSSa0o3HPEGPPIg",
            "text": "ordered list 2"
          }
        ]
      }]
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Unordered List
docs.text:
{
  "id": "S927zAqWQHOkmLEvFespbw",
  "type": "unordered_list",
  "children": [
    {
      "id": "AW53tbxhQYu-HfoSNTfVxQ",
      "type": "list_item",
      "children": [{
        "id": "FZq5VuH8SM-_lE_UKI2GUw",
        "type": "paragraph",
        "children": [
          {
            "id": "NS1OQ71aQ0-VfxtMyqtszw",
            "text": "Unordered list 1"
          }
        ]
      }]
    }, 
    {
      "id": "c-GkcbFsS3uuYNtMgsg2mQ",
      "type": "list_item",
      "children": [{
        "id": "PUoT91gOSoS8hB-HObsD1g",
        "type": "paragraph",
        "children": [
          {
            "id": "QEA-1fOPSSa0o3HPEGPPIg",
            "text": "Unordered list 2"
          }
        ]
      }]
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Multi Column
docs.text: multi_column is a block element node that arranges document content into columns.

docs.title: Children
docs.text:
• Its direct children are column structural elements.
  • A column contains block content, including paragraphs and supported nested blocks such as blockquotes, callouts, lists, and code blocks.
  • A new column starts with a paragraph containing an empty text node. Text and inline elements belong inside its child blocks.

docs.title: Editor-Created Defaults
docs.text:
• column (required for newly-created layouts, array): ordered column metadata.
  • style.gridTemplateColumns (required for newly-created layouts, string): CSS grid column track list, such as repeat(2, 300px) or 250px 350px. This CSS string includes length units.

Each column metadata item has:

  • key (required, string): non-empty identifier matching its child column's id.
  • width (required, number): positive, finite width in CSS pixels (px), without a unit suffix in JSON.
  • left (optional, number): non-negative, finite horizontal layout metadata in CSS pixels (px). Readers can derive column positions from the ordered widths without requiring this field.

Initial widths depend on the available layout width and column count. Historical layouts may use other positive widths.

Each child column has:

  • id (required, string): normally corresponding to the metadata key.
  • type (required): column.
  • width (required for newly-created columns, number): positive, finite width in CSS pixels (px), without a unit suffix in JSON. The editor initializes it from the parent column metadata and prefers the matching metadata width when rendering after layout changes.
  • children (required, array): block content. A new column begins with a paragraph and text leaf.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
  "id": "multi-column-id",
  "type": "multi_column",
  "column": [
    {
      "key": "column-one-id",
      "width": 300,
      "left": 0
    },
    {
      "key": "column-two-id",
      "width": 300,
      "left": 300
    }
  ],
  "style": {
    "gridTemplateColumns": "repeat(2, 300px)"
  },
  "children": [
    {
      "id": "column-one-id",
      "type": "column",
      "width": 300,
      "children": [
        {
          "id": "paragraph-one-id",
          "type": "paragraph",
          "children": [
            {
              "id": "text-one-id",
              "text": "Column one content"
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "column-two-id",
      "type": "column",
      "width": 300,
      "children": [
        {
          "id": "paragraph-two-id",
          "type": "paragraph",
          "children": [
            {
              "id": "text-two-id",
              "text": "Column two content"
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Paragraph
docs.text: paragraph is a block element node that represents a paragraph of rich text.

docs.title: Children
docs.text:
• Its children directly contain text nodes and supported inline elements, such as links, images, file links, and SeaDoc links.
  • Plain text does not require an inline wrapper. A paragraph does not contain other block elements.

docs.title: Data Structure
docs.text:
{
  "id": "afLKcmNdR4ii2ZqvH8PP8w",
  "type": "paragraph",
  "children": [
    {
      "id": "bKfw6ms4QlqUf1J5aFCr4w",
      "text": "text content"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: SeaDoc Link
docs.text: sdoc_link is an inline element node that references another SeaDoc file. It is a void element.

docs.title: Children
docs.text: • Its children contain a text node storing the display name. The editor treats the link as a single unit; the stored display name is not ordinary editable child text.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
• doc_uuid (required, string): referenced SeaDoc file identifier.
  • title (required, string): display title.
  • display_type (required, string): one of text_link (display name only), icon_link (file icon and display name), or card_link (document card). The insertion command creates icon_link by default.

Writers must persist one of these three display modes. For compatibility, a missing or empty display_type is displayed as a text link by the editor; this fallback is different from the insertion default.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
  "id": "sdoc-link-id",
  "type": "sdoc_link",
  "doc_uuid": "c24cee20-88c2-4dba-beb9-4032c5e2c3e1",
  "title": "Project plan",
  "display_type": "text_link",
  "children": [
    {
      "id": "sdoc-link-text-id",
      "text": "Project plan"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Historical documents may retain the .sdoc suffix in title and displayed text. New documents use the suffix-free display form. Compatibility and migration behavior may depend on the reader implementation.

docs.title: Subtitle
docs.text: subtitle is a block element node that represents a document subtitle.

docs.title: Children
docs.text: • Its children directly contain text nodes and supported inline elements, such as links. Content following a subtitle remains in sibling blocks, rather than becoming its children.

docs.title: Data Structure
docs.text:
{
  "id": "G1opTnrHRr6aX7qbJXZJiw",
  "type": "subtitle",
  "children": [
    {
      "id": "D_bLOntqQHSZ8lu9VJn_JQ",
      "text": "subtitle content"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Table
docs.text: table is a block element node that represents content arranged into rows and cells.

docs.title: Usage and Children
docs.text:
• Its direct children are table_row elements, whose children are table_cell elements.
  • Cells directly contain text nodes and supported inline elements, such as links and images. A paragraph wrapper is not required; the editor flattens paragraph children when importing cells.
table -> table_row -> table_cell -> text or inline elements

table_row and table_cell are structural element types.

docs.title: Editor-Created Defaults
docs.text:
A newly-created rectangular table has these layout fields:

  • columns (required for newly-created tables, array): ordered column width metadata. Each item's width is a positive, finite number in CSS pixels (px), without a unit suffix in JSON. Initial widths depend on the available layout width and column count.
  • ui (required for newly-created tables, object): table display metadata such as alternate_highlight.
  • style.gridTemplateColumns (required for newly-created tables, string): CSS grid column track list corresponding to the column metadata, for example repeat(2, 336px) or 300px 372px. This CSS string includes length units.
  • style.gridAutoRows (required for newly-created tables, string): CSS grid row sizing, initially minmax(42px, auto).
  • table_row.style.min_height (required for newly-created rows, number): positive, finite row minimum height in CSS pixels (px), without a unit suffix in JSON. New rows start at 42.
  • table_cell.style (required for newly-created cells, object): cell style.
  • table_cell.inherit_style (required for newly-created cells, object): style inherited by inserted cells.

docs.title: Field Values
docs.text:
• ui.alternate_highlight (boolean): true enables alternating row highlighting; false disables it. The normal table insertion command uses false unless a table template requests highlighting.
  • table_cell.style.text_align (string): horizontal alignment, such as left, center, or right.
  • table_cell.style.align_items (string): vertical alignment, such as flex-start (top), center, or flex-end (bottom).
  • table_cell.style.background_color (string): CSS background color. An absent field or an empty string applies no explicit cell background, allowing table highlighting or the surrounding background to remain visible.

Cell style fields can be absent when no explicit style has been set. inherit_style stores styles to apply when inserting cells; its text_align and background_color fields use the same value conventions as style. Numeric widths and heights are pixel values, while grid layout strings contain CSS length units. Positive saved widths and heights in historical documents need not match editor-created defaults.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
  "id": "table-id",
  "type": "table",
  "columns": [
    { "width": 336 }
  ],
  "ui": {
    "alternate_highlight": false
  },
  "style": {
    "gridTemplateColumns": "repeat(1, 336px)",
    "gridAutoRows": "minmax(42px, auto)"
  },
  "children": [
    {
      "id": "row-id",
      "type": "table_row",
      "style": {
        "min_height": 42
      },
      "children": [
        {
          "id": "cell-id",
          "type": "table_cell",
          "style": {
            "text_align": "left",
            "align_items": "center",
            "background_color": ""
          },
          "inherit_style": {
            "text_align": "left",
            "background_color": ""
          },
          "children": [
            {
              "id": "cell-text-id",
              "text": "Name"
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Historical documents may contain style.alignItems. New documents use style.align_items. Compatibility and migration behavior may depend on the reader implementation.

docs.title: Text
docs.text: A text node is a leaf node that stores text content and optional formatting marks.

docs.title: Children
docs.text:
• Plain text does not require an inline wrapper.
  • Void elements also retain text children as structural placeholders or stored display labels; those children are not ordinary editable text.
  • A text node has no children.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
A text leaf has:

  • id (required, string): unique node identifier.
  • text (required, string): displayed text.

Text leaves do not require type or children.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
  "id": "text-id",
  "text": "Text content"
}

docs.title: Text Formatting (Marks)
docs.text:
Text leaves may carry the following formatting fields:

  • bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, superscript, subscript, and code (optional, boolean): true enables the corresponding mark; false or an absent field leaves it disabled.
  • color (optional, string): CSS text color, such as #ff0000 or rgb(255, 0, 0). An absent field or an empty string applies no explicit text color, so the surrounding style determines the color.
  • highlight_color (optional, string): CSS background color, such as #fff1e8 or rgba(255, 241, 232, 0.5). An absent field or an empty string applies no explicit highlight.
  • font_size (optional, number): positive, finite font size in points (pt), without a unit suffix in JSON. Fractional values are supported. For example, 12 means 12pt, not 12px. An absent field inherits the surrounding font size; the editor's ordinary body-text default is 11pt, while headings and other specialized blocks can use different defaults.
  • font (optional, string): font family name, such as Arial or Noto Sans SC, or default_font for the editor's default font stack. An absent field or an empty string inherits the surrounding font. Font availability and fallback depend on the reader environment.

Serialize font sizes as numbers, rather than strings such as "12pt". Colors may use CSS color representations beyond hexadecimal.

Revision, diff, comment, selection, cursor, AI, and syntax-decoration fields are not ordinary rich-text formatting fields in this specification.

docs.title: Title
docs.text: title is a block element node that represents a document title.

docs.title: Children
docs.text: • Its children directly contain text nodes and supported inline elements, such as links. Content following a title remains in sibling blocks, rather than becoming its children.

docs.title: Data Structure
docs.text:
{
  "id": "G1opTnrHRr6aX7qbJXZJiw",
  "type": "title",
  "children": [
    {
      "id": "D_bLOntqQHSZ8lu9VJn_JQ",
      "text": "title content"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Video
docs.text: video is a block element node that represents an uploaded video or an embeddable video link. It is a void element.

docs.title: Children
docs.text: • Its children contain one empty text node as a structural placeholder. The video source and display settings belong in data, rather than editable child text. See Void Elements.

docs.title: Required Properties
docs.text:
• data (required, object): video data.
  • data.src (required, string): non-empty video source. Uploaded videos use an asset path or an absolute HTTP(S) URL. When data.is_embeddable_link is true, this is the provider's embeddable-player URL, rather than its ordinary watch-page URL.

docs.title: Optional Properties
docs.text:
• data.name (optional, string or null): video filename or display name. When absent, null, or empty, the editor uses data.src as the display name.
  • data.size (optional, number or null): non-negative integer size in bytes. An absent field or null means the size is unknown, rather than zero bytes.
  • data.is_embeddable_link (optional, boolean): true renders src in an embedded player; false renders it as a video file. An absent field behaves as false.
  • data.width (optional, number): positive, finite display width in CSS pixels (px), without a unit suffix in JSON. When omitted, the editor uses 100% of the available container width.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
  "id": "video-id",
  "type": "video",
  "data": {
    "src": "/video.mp4",
    "name": "video.mp4",
    "size": 2357967,
    "is_embeddable_link": false,
    "width": 640
  },
  "children": [
    {
      "id": "video-placeholder-id",
      "text": ""
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Whiteboard
docs.text: whiteboard is a block element node that references a whiteboard file. It is a void element.

docs.title: Children
docs.text: • Its children contain one empty text node as a structural placeholder. The file reference and display information belong in the element's properties, rather than editable child text. See Void Elements.

docs.title: Required Properties
docs.text:
• repo_id (required, string): repository identifier containing the whiteboard file.
  • title (required, string): whiteboard filename or display title.
  • file_path (required, string): path to the whiteboard file.
  • link (required, string): read-only whiteboard link.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
  "id": "whiteboard-id",
  "type": "whiteboard",
  "repo_id": "repo-id",
  "title": "Architecture.exdraw",
  "file_path": "/Design/Architecture.exdraw",
  "link": "https://example.com/whiteboard/read-only-link",
  "children": [
    {
      "id": "whiteboard-placeholder-id",
      "text": ""
    }
  ]
}
